questions.q_figure: Table 1 listing ten number sequences with their first terms: All 1's, Counting numbers, Odd numbers, Even numbers, Triangular numbers, Squares, Cubes, Virahanka numbers, Powers of 2 and Powers of 3, each written as a row of numbers followed by three dots.

Table 2 with seven rows of pictures, five pictures in each row and every picture labelled with its number: All 1's as single dots (1), Counting numbers as rows of dots (1 to 5), Odd numbers as dot patterns (1, 3, 5, 7, 9), Even numbers as dot patterns (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), Triangular numbers as dot triangles (1, 3, 6, 10, 15), Squares as dot squares (1, 4, 9, 16, 25) and Cubes as stacks of coloured unit blocks (1, 8, 27, 64, 125).
questions.s_figure: The sixth picture of each sequence: a single dot, a row of 6 dots, 11 dots in the odd-number pattern, 12 dots in two rows of 6, a triangle of 21 dots in rows of 1 to 6, a 6 by 6 square of 36 dots and a 6 by 6 by 6 cube of 216 blocks.
A triangle of 10 dots in rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4, a 4 by 4 square of 16 dots and a 3 by 3 by 3 cube of 27 unit blocks, side by side.
The same 36 dots drawn twice: as a triangle with rows of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 dots, and as a 6 by 6 square.

questions.q_figure: Four hexagon-shaped clusters of red dots in a row, labelled 1, 7, 19 and 37 below them.
questions.s_figure: The four clusters followed by the next cluster of 61 dots, a centre dot with four rings of dots around it.

Powers of 2 drawn as a point, a line segment, a square, a cube and a four-dimensional cube for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, each made of two copies of the one before joined at their corners; Powers of 3 drawn as a dot, a triangle of 3 dots, three triangles joined and three of those joined.

questions.q_figure: Table 3 with five rows of shape sequences: Regular Polygons (triangle to decagon), Complete Graphs (K2 to K6), Stacked Squares, Stacked Triangles and the Koch Snowflake, each row showing its first shapes from left to right.

Table 3 with five rows of shape sequences: Regular Polygons (triangle to decagon), Complete Graphs (K2 to K6), Stacked Squares, Stacked Triangles and the Koch Snowflake, each row showing its first shapes from left to right.
The Regular Polygons row of Table 3: a triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon and decagon in a row.
The Complete Graphs row of Table 3: K2 to K6, each a set of points with a line joining every pair of points, from a single line for K2 to a hexagon with all its diagonals for K6.
The Stacked Squares row of Table 3: five shapes made of little squares, a single small square followed by larger and larger square blocks of little squares.
The Stacked Triangles row of Table 3: five triangles made of little triangles, a single small triangle followed by larger and larger triangles divided into little triangles.
The Koch Snowflake row of Table 3: five shapes, a triangle then a six-pointed star then shapes with finer and finer bumps along every edge.
